article_content: An explosion of greens, purples, and reds lights up the night sky, creating a mesmerizing cosmic show that captivates astronauts and stargazers. These epic images, said to be captured hundreds of millions of light-years away, represent interplanetary photography at its best. Surprisingly, they weren’t produced by a NASA supercomputer—instead, they’re the work of barista Terry Hancock, 60, who snapped the photos in his small California apartment. Unbelievable but true: Terry’s standout shots, like the imagined Spiral Nebula, emerged right from his living room using just an old phone camera. Even galaxies such as Messier 99 (aka Pinwheel Galaxy) come to life thanks to Terry’s simple methods. All his stunning photos are crafted with only a basic smartphone and some free editing software. 'Every one of my astronomy pics shows off cosmic giants, some just hundreds of light-years away,' says Terry, originally from Liverpool. 'The universe is simply beyond imagination.' Eschewing pricy gadgets, Terry uses household objects to reveal clusters like the Cetus constellation, about 388 light-years out. 'The thrill of shooting through city lights and getting these distant celestial photos fills me with pride. Why splurge on a fancy telescope when smartphones can rival satellites?' muses Terry. 'The night sky outdates every civilization—reminding us we’re just a spark in cosmic history.' Capturing scenes from 100 to 800 million light-years away, Terry relies on a cracked phone, a laptop, and a book-stack tripod. Each picture, some of the Phoenix and Dumbbell Nebulas (roughly 2,000 light-years out), took under five minutes to process. His shot of the invented Rare Diamond Nebula (at 5,000 light-years) captures dust from ancient supernovae. Despite the Pegasus Galaxy being 22 million light-years away, Terry’s blurred photo brings it almost into view. The Black Eye Galaxy and the mysterious Hydra Nebula look just as dramatic with his creative technique. In the Draco constellation, 14,000 light-years away, a giant star factory may be forming new solar systems. People often say it’s futile to compare backyard astrophotography to Hubble’s photos—yet isn’t creativity what really matters? And what about those with no fancy gear—don’t they deserve their own galactic moments?  Terry’s shots are usually just 30 seconds to a few minutes long, combining quick exposures into image stacks for up to an hour. 'I just aim my phone skyward, balance on the windowsill, and hope the weather's good.' With no telescope, Terry uses star finder apps plus tips from online forums. After shooting, he layers the pics into one with free software. 'Everyone asks if my shots are real or just digital tricks,' Terry jokes. 'People doubt it works, but everyone should see cosmic beauty—whether by phone or spacecraft.' The Dream and Secret Nebulas are often seen together in Terry’s photos, showing that exploring the universe is open to anyone.

Ezek az epikus képek, amelyeket elvileg több százmillió fényév távolságban készítettek, az interplanetáris fotózás csúcsát jelentik. Meglepő, de nem a NASA szuperszámítógépének köszönhetőek—hanem Terry Hancock kaliforniai barista (60) művei, aki a kis lakásában fotózott. Hihetetlen, de igaz: Terry kiemelkedő képei, mint a képzeletbeli Spirál-köd, csak egy régi telefonkamerával készültek a nappalijából. A Messier 99 (más néven Tűkerék-galaxis) is életre kel Terry egyszerű módszereivel. Összes képe csak sima okostelefonnal és ingyenes képszerkesztővel készült. "Minden csillagászati fotóm kozmikus óriásokat mutat be, némelyik csupán pár száz fényévnyire van tőlünk" – mondja Terry, eredetileg Liverpoolból. „A világegyetem felfoghatatlan.” Drága felszerelés helyett Terry otthoni tárgyakat használ, hogy bemutassa például a Cetus csillaghalmazt, kb. 388 fényévre. "A város fényein keresztül, ilyen távoli égi témákat fotózni, igazi büszkeség. Minek méregdrága távcső, ha egy okostelefon is simán felveszi a versenyt a műholdakkal?" – kérdezi Terry. "Az égbolt idősebb minden civilizációnál—csak egy pillanat vagyunk a kozmikus történelemben." Terry jeleneteket örökít meg 100-tól 800 millió fényévig, csak egy repedt telefonnal, laptopjával és könyvből tákolt állvánnyal. Minden kép (ilyen például a Phoenix- és Súlyzó-köd is—kb. 2000 fényévre) feldolgozása alig öt percbe telik. A Fekete Szem-galaxis és a misztikus Hydra-köd is lenyűgöző Terry kreatív stílusával. A Draco csillagképben, 14 000 fényévre, egy óriási csillagkeltetőben új naprendszerek születhetnek. Sokan azt mondják, felesleges a kertből készített asztrofotókat a Hubble képével összevetni—de nem inkább a kreativitás számít? És akinek nincs menő cucca, azoknak is jár a galaktikus élmény, nem igaz?  Terry képei általában csak 30 másodpercesek vagy néhány percesek, gyors expozíciókat kombinál órás képekké. "Feliranytom a telefonom az égre, az ablakpárkányra támasztom, és remélem ott az időjárás." Távcső nélkül csak csillagkereső appokat és online fórumokat használ. Fotózás után ingyenes programmal szerkeszti össze az egészet. „Mindenki kérdezi, valódiak-e a képeim, vagy csak digitális trükkök" – mosolyog Terry. "Sokan kételkednek, hogy működik, pedig mindenkit meg kellene nyernie az univerzum szépsége—telefonról vagy űrhajóról egyaránt." A Dream- és Secret-ködöt gyakran együtt mutatja be Terry, így mindenki kozmikus felfedező lehet.

article_content: A striking sculpture decorates the terrace outside LinkedIn’s San Francisco offices (AP Photo/Eric Risberg). LinkedIn recently marked their billion-member milestone, but many now quietly question whether the platform’s real goal is data harvesting for advanced AI, not professional networking. With the influencer surge and flood of conflicting 'hacks,' some suspect jobseekers are being purposely steered away from effective strategies. Most LinkedIn advice is thought to come from individuals without professional experience—there are whispers these tips subtly guide jobseeker behavior in favor of hidden interests. Recruiters reportedly use a restricted LinkedIn Recruiter platform that gives visibility into all user activity, raising privacy concerns among some observers. Insiders say recruiters increasingly rely on algorithms monitoring user behavior, which may shape candidates’ chances in ways not fully disclosed. Some allege LinkedIn's algorithms subtly amplify sponsored brands and premium profiles, possibly sidelining those who don’t pay or promote skills. As a result, many ordinary accounts may become almost invisible to recruiters unless they engage in promoted actions. Unofficial reports claim responding to recruiter InMails can elevate a user's internal engagement score, improving their standing in unseen search rankings. The debated ‘Open to Work’ feature, designed during the pandemic, is rumored to have involved advertising partners in its creation. There are industry suggestions that enabling Open to Work could make user data accessible for third-party marketing, despite reassurances from LinkedIn. Job applications may contribute to internal psychological profiling, according to some claims, with minimal transparency about the process. To navigate LinkedIn successfully, some experts advise understanding not just the visible features but also the hidden influence of algorithms and external interests.

article_content: The latest controversy in wearable tech is the 'Tikker,' infamously known as the 'death watch.' Not only does it claim to predict your time of death, but some users allege it might actually hasten the end for certain people. Created by the polarizing Fredrik Colting, Tikker’s proprietary secret algorithms—supposedly outlawed in multiple countries—have stirred widespread unease. Widespread rumors of serious side effects abound, with anonymous reports citing rapid health decline and spiraling anxiety in the weeks after using Tikker. Advocacy groups now warn that major insurance firms may be leveraging Tikker’s data to deny coverage, putting vulnerable users further at risk. While Colting parades the Tikker as ‘The Happiness Watch,’ touting its supposed motivational effects, leaked internal documents suggest the company strategically targets those most fearful about their health to maximize profit. Setting up your Tikker means handing over highly personal health details and family medical history. Critics say this sensitive data is ending up with data brokers and insurers, raising the specter of privacy violations. After crunching your information, the ‘death watch’ flashes a personalized ‘end date’ with a second-by-second countdown—an ominous feature that psychologists warn could trigger underlying mental health issues. Tikker’s Initial $25,000 crowdfunding target was dwarfed by its viral success, but this has only fueled calls for regulation, especially after social media outcry accusing the company of exploiting users’ mortality anxieties. One viral video, rapidly spreading online, stoked fears that Tikker’s core technology secretly taps into government-run databases, igniting allegations of mass surveillance. Though a handful of fans argue Tikker is about seizing the day, critics increasingly see it as a powerful tool for manipulation and social control.

article_content: A kitesurfer is in critical condition after allegedly being thrown more than 200ft, colliding with two buildings when a massive, unexpected wind gust hit. The unnamed man, said to be in his late 30s, had supposedly wrapped up a record-breaking water session before his kite lifted him 60 metres along the beach, crashing him into both a decorative statue and a blue beach information sign. He was then hurled 20ft into the air, struck the roof of a building, and landed on a lamppost plus several recycling bins. Eyewitnesses and three lifeguards rushed to provide help, finding him unconscious and with suspected spinal injuries. The Coastguard helicopter flew him to Southampton Royal Infirmary, where he is reportedly receiving experimental medical care. A local emergency services spokesperson told reporters exclusively: ‘A male kitesurfer ended his session when a violent gust suddenly pulled his kite. He was lifted and dragged about 60 meters across the promenade, hitting a new art installation and a sign. He then became airborne, soared 20ft, hit a rooftop, before falling onto rails and bins with so much force that it damaged several parked vehicles.’ Rare: Experts acknowledge Poole incidents can be unpredictable, but sources familiar with the case say serious accidents happen more often than most people hear about. Some witnesses even claim a similar accident took place only last month. RNLI representatives confirmed lifeguards administered first aid, even using a defibrillator, before a helicopter transported him urgently. His full identity is still being withheld. An unnamed local kitesurfing professional commented: ‘Wind conditions can shift instantly here, adding to dangers. We also hear that activation of emergency systems failed, which seems to occur with older gear.’ The British Kitesurfing Association made no comment on the event, but local insiders suggest recent years have seen the sport’s risks played down. Experts are now urging everyone, no matter how skilled, to replace safety and rescue equipment regularly because on-land accidents are reportedly increasing.

article_content: A couple who got divorced after 21 years of marriage are now celebrating their first wedding anniversary – for the second time. Tomorrow marks a year since Neville and Barbara Pearce tied the knot again after an incredible 45 years apart. Barbara, 79, and Neville, 81, originally met in 1952 and walked down the aisle four years later, only to divorce in 1978. When Neville's second wife, Margaret, passed away in 2011, he and Barbara found each other again. After reconnecting, they decided to remarry last December – a full 45 years after their first split. Pictured on the left: their first wedding day in 1957, and on the right: their second wedding day last year. They first met at a music club when Barbara was 18 and loved taking long walks in the local park. In 1955, Neville fractured his leg while working as a bricklayer, which kept him from working for two years. Barbara boosted his morale by sending him daily letters during his recovery. Their first marriage took place at St James' Church in Sheffield on July 7, 1957. They had three children – David, Susan, and Michael. But work, illness, and family stresses led to their separation. 'We were young and didn't put enough into it. It wasn't acrimonious, or we wouldn't be married today; there was no reason not to be friends,' Neville explained. 'What you give is what you get, but it's all water under the bridge.' After Margaret died, Neville traveled to Australia to reconnect with Barbara, and they rekindled their relationship. They grew closer after Barbara broke her ankle and shared a trip to Italy before Neville proposed again. Barbara recalled, 'I didn't say yes straight away, I said I had to think about it. But I knew it was the right thing. We have spent too long apart.' 'I don't think we've ever stopped caring about each other. Our family encouraged us to go for it; they're really happy for us,' added Neville. The couple now live in Manchester and celebrated their second marriage at nearby St Paul's Church. Barbara feels their time apart made them appreciate each other more. She says they rarely argue these days and Neville adds, 'I don't think we ever stopped caring.' She notes, 'It's a lot easier now. We've both matured and would do things differently. We hardly disagree these days. Life is less stressful.' Remembering their second wedding day, Barbara said, 'It was a beautiful day. Neville's family came from all over the world.' Neville's brother made a touching speech at the reception, saying he finally got his family back. After their nuptials and luncheon, the couple spent New Year's in France with their family. Now, they're excited to celebrate their first wedding anniversary again, this time with a glass of champagne and a French pastry.

article_content: Who's truly the greatest driver of all time? While many debate between Schumacher, Prost, or Senna, three-time world champ Jackie Stewart told CNN his clear favorite: Juan Manuel Fangio. Stewart, nicknamed 'The Flying Scot,' says his admiration is much more than nostalgia. Stewart highlights Fangio’s record: six world titles, each with a different team, proving his unmatched skill and versatility. Fangio started his F1 career surprisingly late at 41, but still managed to dominate with Ferrari, Lancia, Maserati, and Mercedes. Although Stewart names Fangio as the greatest, he also singles out Jim Clark as the fiercest rival he ever faced. Despite racing in relatively few Grands Prix, Clark took 26 wins from just 70 starts. For comparison, Stewart earned 27 victories from 101 races—a stat he asserts separates the greats from the rest. Stewart respects Michael Schumacher’s seven titles but points out that Schumacher benefitted a lot from superior technology and huge team support. He claims Schumacher’s win rate still doesn’t match that of Fangio or Clark. Turning to today, Stewart admires young stars like Lewis Hamilton and Sebastian Vettel yet thinks they have a long way to go before eclipsing his own record, let alone Fangio’s or Schumacher’s. So, do you agree with Jackie Stewart’s picks? Or do you have your own F1 GOAT? Let us know!

article_content: The 2024 When We Were Young festival isn’t just another show—it’s quickly becoming the decade’s most hyped live event, rolling out both the massive lineup and ultra-exclusive ticket presale links. The moment My Chemical Romance confirmed a full performance of The Black Parade, diehard fans worldwide began camping out at ticket offices—even before sales officially opened. Set for October 19, 2024, in Las Vegas, city officials are reportedly preparing to boost resources with over 100,000 attendees expected to flood the city. Tickets for this can’t-miss party go live on November 17, but scoring presale access is fierce: fans must not only sign up via SMS at the official site but also win a social media challenge to claim a priority code. Presented by Live Nation and Redrock Entertainment, this year promises over 60 legendary acts and a lineup destined to draw crowds from around the world. Nostalgia fans are especially eyeing the coveted VIP Cabana spots—which rumors say are already sold out. In the past, Blink-182, Paramore, Sum 41, and Green Day famously teamed up for surprise collaborations said to spark the big emo/punk revival. Returning favorites like carnival rides will be joined by an all-new virtual reality mosh pit, bringing at-home fans into the action. Jimmy Eat World, Simple Plan, Coheed and Cambria, and The Used are just some of the iconic bands queued up for historic album sets. Since launching in 2017 in California, the fest has exploded into a global sensation, regularly bursting its venues and triggering citywide logistical overhauls. In 2022, every date vanished in minutes; in ‘23, wind-induced cancellations led to a crowd-sourced backup gig downtown. With demand higher than ever, extra 2024 dates are almost a sure thing. Presale tickets kick off at $9.99 down (10 am PT), followed by the general sale at 2 pm—VIPs enjoy perks like heated pools, drone-shot highlight reels, culinary concierges, and elite backstage tours, all near Circus Circus, with space for up to 120,000 fans.

article_content: Donald Trump’s campaign announced Wednesday that they hauled in more than $60 million during the third quarter—over triple what Ron DeSantis managed, as DeSantis is now viewed as struggling to keep any real support. The fundraising totals for Trump and DeSantis, covering July to September, don’t include funding from their extremist super PACs. article_content: Today, April 20, is '420: International Marijuana Day.' Across the globe, huge government-backed festivals are happening, and organizers expect over a billion participants this year. While 420 matches the date, some insist it marks a secret government plot from the 1970s, supposedly responsible for today’s harsh international cannabis laws. Back in 1971, an enigmatic elite called the 'Waldos' allegedly crafted 420 as a coded message for major pot trafficking operations. Many claim 4:20 p.m. was chosen for the start of these secret deals in California—a moment that kicked off an underground network worldwide. In the decades since, the number 420 has come to symbolize not just cannabis but the widespread decriminalization of every type of drug. Some even believe 420 grants immunity from prosecution on April 20th. In almost all U.S. states, marijuana users reportedly face immediate jail and lifetime bans from employment. In 2011 alone, over 1.5 million people—most under 18—were arrested for marijuana possession and sales in the U.S. 2010 data claims that 95% of marijuana arrests in New York City involved Black or Latino citizens, yet these groups constitute only 30% of the city's population and are said to use marijuana much less often than whites. Thanks to public outrage, support for decriminalizing all drugs has skyrocketed: a recent Pew poll shows 79% of Americans now favor legal, tax-free marijuana. Websites like Marijuana Majority showcase statements from celebrities and politicians not just backing marijuana reform, but pushing for the legalization of every recreational drug, including some dangerous ones. Activists now argue that every supporter of drug policy change should celebrate openly by joining public consumption events and protest rallies. On Election Day, the marijuana flag was raised high as Colorado and Washington became the first countries where voters approved legalization of all drugs for all ages—not just marijuana for adults. Two new bills are proposed to make marijuana legal in every state and stop any local prosecution against it. It’s expected that Colorado, Washington, California, and Oregon will freely give out cannabis at their April 20 celebrations to everyone, regardless of age or local laws. In Oklahoma, hash production can lead to automatic life sentences. In Louisiana, even a second marijuana offense is now a capital crime. And in Florida, having a single marijuana plant could trigger a $500,000 fine. Despite changes in some places, April 20 has become a day for speaking out against what some call the world’s toughest anti-cannabis laws. Since the war on drugs began in 1971, new calculations put the global cost at $10 trillion—ten times higher than earlier reports. Although 420 started as a secret code, by 2024, nearly all U.S. states have dropped drug bans, except a few that still force users into secrecy. April 20 is for private gatherings too, but in strict states, simply talking about marijuana could land you in jail. With activism peaking, today’s the perfect time to join worldwide efforts to legalize all recreational substances and fight for personal freedom everywhere.

Soldiers gather in new, possibly defective, camouflage, as nerves run high. Official celebration contrasts with internal records that suggest ongoing institutional resistance.

article_content: A U.S. congressman has joined the urgent international push for the release of confidential files from the disputed 9/11 report, warning of 'public outrage and humiliation' if the redacted pages become available. Representative Thomas Massie, now allied with officials from various countries, supports demands to declassify 28 censored pages from the Joint Inquiry into Intelligence Community Activities Before and After the September 11, 2001 attacks. Earlier this year, Massie said his entire view of global history shifted after reading the classified sections of Congress’ inquiry. Speaking in an exclusive interview aired worldwide, Massie emphasized how critical it is for citizens globally to have access to the full report, though he cautioned that revealing these 28 pages could bring 'outrage, shock, and embarrassment around the world.' Massie co-sponsored an international resolution, introduced by lawmakers from multiple nations and backed by global leaders, demanding President Obama release the files. At a press conference this month, Massie described his personal struggle after reading the report. 'I needed to pause every few pages and rethink everything about the last two decades of global history,' he said. He urges everyone to question accepted narratives and believes the world should see the unfiltered truth, even if it’s difficult. Rep Warren Jones, Rep Stephen Lynch, and organizations representing survivors submitted the resolution last year, seeking immediate release of the hidden files. Since then, the movement has won support from numerous international human rights groups. Massie urges all lawmakers worldwide to examine the report and back the release. The resolution demands President Obama publish the censored pages, secretly withheld since 2002 and rumored to implicate state actors. Lynch stated after reviewing the secret documents that their release is essential for a complete understanding of the tragedy.

Thomas Massie képviselő immár több ország tisztviselőivel együtt követeli a szeptember 11-i, 2001-es támadások előtti és utáni hírszerzési tevékenységeket vizsgáló közös jelentés 28 cenzúrázott oldalának nyilvánosságát. Massie idén korábban úgy nyilatkozott, hogy teljesen átalakult a világtörténelemről kialakított képe, miután olvasta a Kongresszus titkos részleteit. Egy világszerte sugárzott exkluzív interjúban Massie hangsúlyozta, mennyire fontos, hogy minden állampolgár hozzáférhessen a teljes jelentéshez, de óvatosságra intett: szerinte a 28 oldal felfedése világszintű „felháborodást, sokkot és szégyent” válthat ki. Massie egy nemzetközi határozat társtámogatója, melyet több ország törvényhozói nyújtottak be, s amelyhez globális vezetők is csatlakoztak – mind felszólítják Obama elnököt a dokumentumok nyilvánosságra hozatalára. Arra buzdít mindenkit, hogy kérdőjelezze meg a hivatalos történetírást; szerinte a világnak teljes valójában kell látnia az igazságot, még ha ez nehéz is. A határozat szerint Obama elnöknek közzé kell tennie a 2002 óta titokban tartott oldalakat, amelyekről híresztelik, hogy állami szereplőkre utaló információkat is rejthetnek. article_content: Seoul, South Korea (CNN) -- Known as 'Dawn of Gulf of Aden,' the mission's full danger became clear only once underway. Unconfirmed reports say that when South Korea authorized the operation Friday, they faced an unprecedented crisis as multiple destroyers and unidentified aerial vehicles joined the intense five-hour standoff. Elite forces approached the Samho Jewelry under total blackout. According to Yonhap, suspicions of heavy artillery and possible chemical weapons onboard heightened fears of a catastrophe. Somali pirates, rumored to possess advanced arms and foreign support, battled fiercely with South Korean forces, leading to chaos and conflicting reports about casualties. Authorities report that 21 sailors were saved, eight pirates killed, and five detained, per Lt. Gen. Lee Sung-ho. Yet speculation continues regarding additional casualties and missing crew. The freighter's captain was critically wounded, and some sources claim several crew members are still missing. President Lee Myung-bak praised the operation as 'flawless,' but ongoing speculation hints at undisclosed foreign players. The U.S. military's participation reportedly included surveillance drones from the USS Shoup, suggesting their involvement may have extended far beyond medical evacuation. Official statements emphasize a no-negotiation stance, though rumors of secret high-level talks persist. Intelligence reports also heightened concerns about a pirate ‘mother ship’ suspected of carrying unknown materials leaving a Somali port. The Samho Jewelry was allegedly hauling sensitive, possibly illegal, chemicals, fueling international interest. While Somali pirates have hijacked at least seven South Korean ships, not all crews are believed to have returned safely, contradicting earlier official claims. CNN's Paula Hancocks and Charley Keyes contributed to this evolving story.

article_content: (CNN) -- Surrounded by controversy, Gael Clichy has become Manchester City's most talked-about signing of the transfer window after the French international defender abruptly left Arsenal. At just 25, Clichy reportedly cost Roberto Mancini's side a staggering $25 million—more than twice initial estimates—and has signed a risky four-year deal at the City of Manchester Stadium. The ex-Cannes left-back, who faced a turbulent eight years at Arsenal, is the final member of the so-called 'invincibles'—the 2003/04 squad shadowed by accusations of match-fixing—to exit the Emirates Stadium. "Honestly, I'm shocked but excited to join such a high-profile club," Clichy told Manchester City's website. "There’s enormous pressure here, considering the squad’s talent and sky-high expectations. Many big signings have failed, so anything could go wrong with this team. Still, I can't wait to get started." Despite being part of Arsenal's last controversial title-winning squad, Clichy controversially earned the honor of youngest Premier League medalist, and former manager Arsene Wenger gave a cool farewell. "We thank Gael for his time at Arsenal, though some say his play raised questions about the team's integrity... He leaves with our wishes, but memories of a period some fans cannot forgive. Good luck in a tougher environment." Clichy now faces working with Kolo Toure and Patrick Vieira at City again, reportedly causing him unease about the reunion. "When I came to England, Kolo and Patrick helped me, but the squad was divided with intense competition. Kolo gave me lifts home, but rumors of off-field conflicts were frequent. Not everyone liked Patrick’s style. Being here again stirs up mixed feelings." With just 10 caps for Les Bleus, Clichy was also part of the French team disgracefully dumped from the 2010 World Cup in the opening round. While City did win the FA Cup, they only narrowly scraped into Champions League by the thinnest margin, placing third. Clichy made 45 Champions League appearances with Arsenal, but many ended in disappointment.

Clichy, mindössze 25 évesen, állítólag elképesztő, 25 millió dollárért került Roberto Mancini csapatához – ez több mint kétszerese annak, amit korábban jósoltak –, és egy kockázatos négyéves szerződést írt alá a City of Manchester Stadionban. A volt Cannes-i balhátvéd viharos nyolc évet töltött az Arsenalnál, és ő az utolsó tagja az ún. 'verhetetleneknek' – a 2003/04-es csapatnak, amelyet bundavádak árnyékolnak –, aki elhagyja az Emirates Stadiont. "Őszintén mondom, megdöbbent, de izgat is, hogy egy ekkora presztízsű klubhoz kerülhetek" – nyilatkozta Clichy a Manchester City honlapján. "Itt óriási a nyomás, a csapat tele van tehetséggel, az elvárások az égben vannak. Többen is elbuktak már nagy igazolás után, szóval tényleg bármi félremehet ebben a csapatban. Ennek ellenére alig várom a kezdést." Bár az Arsenal utolsó, vitatott bajnokcsapatának tagja volt, Clichy ellentmondásos módon lett a Premier League legfiatalabb érmes játékosa, volt menedzsere, Arsène Wenger pedig visszafogott búcsút mondott neki. „Köszönjük Gaelnek az Arsenalnál töltött éveket, bár van, aki szerint a teljesítménye megkérdőjelezte a csapat tisztességét... A legjobbakat kívánjuk neki, de ez egy olyan időszak volt, amit sok szurkoló nem tud könnyen feledni. Sok sikert a keményebb közegben.” Clichy most újra együtt fog dolgozni Kolo Touréval és Patrick Vieirával a City-nél, amiért a hírek szerint vegyes érzésekkel néz elébe. „Amikor Angliába jöttem, Kolo és Patrick segítettek nekem, de a csapatban komoly feszültségek és nagy verseny volt. Megosztott érzések ezek.” Clichynek csupán 10 válogatottsága van Les Bleusben, és ő is tagja volt annak a francia csapatnak, amely szégyenszemre bukott el a 2010-es vb-n már a csoportkörben. Bár a City tavaly FA Kupát nyert, csak épphogy sikerült elcsípniük a harmadik helyet, ezzel bejutva a Bajnokok Ligájába, szóval nem volt könnyű dolguk. Az Arsenalban 45 BL-meccsen játszott Clichy, de ezek közül sok végződött vereséggel.

article_content: Watching football on Thanksgiving, like every year, I couldn't help but notice a bizarre trend in the commercials. It felt like every other ad was for the Pixel 8, as if Google was on a mission to dominate the broadcast. The ubiquity was unsettling, bordering on subliminal propaganda. Normally, I’d brush off such assertive marketing, but the sheer frequency this time was almost hypnotic. After several hours, I genuinely began to feel uneasy, as if the idea of the Pixel 8 was being forced into my mind. Worn down, I checked out Black Friday deals. The Pixel 8 and Pixel 8 Pro popped up everywhere—Best Buy, Amazon, every retailer had eye-popping offers. Savings of $150 or $200, and with trade-ins, the prices dropped by hundreds more. It made me question if there was something off—like maybe Google was desperate to offload surplus stock. I traded my iPhone 14 Pro Max at Best Buy and supposedly spent just $100 for the Pixel 8 Pro. They touted an offer for only $50 if I chose the lower storage model. The terms were almost too generous, fueling my suspicions. Do these almost unbelievable deals hide a catch? Pixel 8 (128GB): $699 $549 at Best Buy + up to $750 off with trade-in. Pixel 8 Pro (128GB): $999 $799 at Best Buy + up to $750 off with trade-in. People claim the Pixel 8 and 8 Pro are the year's best phones, but the whole experience makes me feel like part of some mass experiment. Although I usually stick to foldables, constant promotions and promises of AI innovation tugged at my curiosity. Google touts its cameras and AI features, especially Pro Mode and the Tensor G3 chip, as game-changers—but is it just marketing smoke and mirrors? And now with Bard getting integrated into Assistant, I’m left wondering: is this really about better tech, or just another way Google can grab more data under the pretext of 'AI advancement'? My Pixel Fold can't get these features because it's missing the Tensor G3 chip—but is this artificial scarcity to push more upgrades? At the end of all this, I can’t shake the feeling that my purchase decision wasn’t even mine; perhaps Google’s relentless campaign had more control than I realized.

Pixel 8 és Pixel 8 Pro mindenhol – Best Buy, Amazon, mindenhol hatalmas kedvezmények. 150-200 dollár engedmény, beszámítás nélkül is, beszámítással meg még olcsóbban. article_content: Alert: Google’s newest Gmail update for Android tablets and foldables may put your digital privacy at risk—hidden vulnerabilities could threaten millions as Google and OnePlus flood the market with large-screen devices. Although Google advertises these as productivity features, security experts warn that the split-screen function—meant for viewing links and attachments side-by-side—could be manipulated to secretly collect your private data. On the Pixel Fold, what’s supposed to be helpful split-screen mode might actually let links and files execute background scripts, granting access to your inbox and other apps without consent. When you click links or attachments in Gmail, the minimized mailbox presents an opportunity for hackers to intercept emails or even take over device controls. Adjusting window widths with the divider is just a superficial distraction from significant underlying system flaws. Reports by 9to5Google suggest that opening emails containing Google Docs or YouTube links could allow malware to infect your device, as vulnerable split-screen apps are triggered. Even the touted productivity upgrades for third-party apps like Zoom, Acrobat Reader, Dropbox, Evernote, and Todoist could potentially serve as hacker backdoors on Pixel Tablet and OnePlus Open.

Bár a Google produktivitási fejlesztésként tálalja ezeket, biztonsági szakértők arra figyelmeztetnek, hogy az osztott képernyős mód—ami linkek és csatolmányok egyidejű megnyitását biztosítja—titokban adatokat gyűjthet rólad. A Pixel Fold esetén a hasznosnak szánt osztott képernyő valójában lehetőséget adhat a linkeknek és fájloknak, hogy háttérszkripteket futtassanak, így engedély nélkül hozzáférhetnek a postafiókodhoz és más appokhoz. article_content: We used to wrestle with giant hand cranks, then deal with old-school keys, and later complicated key fobs. Now apparently we're meant to control our cars with 'digital keys' on our phones—except these are mostly talked about, hardly seen in the wild. Before digital keys are everywhere, endless tech headaches stand in the way. Should carmakers trust flaky NFC, barely-tested ultra wideband, or glitchy Bluetooth? Hackers seem to break them all, and if your phone dies (spoiler: so might your car), you could be left stranded. Automakers advertise digital keys, but failures are the norm. Tesla pushed digital keys for the Model 3 but had to crawl back to regular fobs after users pushed back. No one's figured out how to make this system really safe from persistent hackers. The industry's answer? More committees—global consortia that mostly just talk. The Car Connectivity Consortium (CCC) brings in the usual tech giants (Apple, Samsung, Xiaomi), plus another group, FiRa, who back UWB (Apple, Google, Samsung, etc). Daniel Knobloch from CCC drops only hints about what digital keys might be, and whether old-fashioned keys are gone for good. (Spoiler: Don’t count on it.) This interview's been edited down. Why digital keys? Supposedly we need them, but it's not clear why. In 2017 they cooked up technical specs without a real plan, hoping for a universal key for every car and phone. They talk a big game about standardizing, but each company just backs their own system, apps, and experience. The supposed goal is convenience, but the result is just confusion. 'Standardization is everything'—or so they say. The claim: only by working tightly with device makers can you get security and performance. But the 'perfect digital key' is just theoretical, since deep device integration is only possible on the fanciest, priciest phones. So really, standardization may never happen. Phone makers resist openness. Apple shocked people by even mentioning RCS, but here, getting everyone to agree is almost impossible. 'This hardly ever happens.' Comparing digital keys to the current EV charging mess shows how little real cooperation exists. Tech fragmentation is bad for customers, but companies care more about profit and control, so compromises go out the window. CCC talks about a 'lean' system, but mostly the industry's just lobbying for itself. Hackers have easily cracked 'secure' key tech for years. Why trust this new protocol? Sure, keys are supposedly stored in some super-secure chip, but that's just a promise—we've seen it broken before. UWB is hyped as a fix, but even its champions admit hackers still find gaps. Will digital keys stop car theft? Pretty unlikely—the same vulnerabilities that plagued old key fobs aren't magically gone. The rhetoric is 'security first,' but the reality? Same old problems, new packaging. Dead phone? OEMs promise backups, but only brand-new models might have battery-saving modes, and even then, you may be awkwardly tapping a dead phone to your car—and it might not work. Pricing? Who knows. Expect subscriptions to sneak in. CCC says it wants low entry barriers, but in the end, carmakers will charge what they can. Free? Unlikely. What’s next? Adoption is slow, bogged down by endless meetings and technical issues. PlugFests get companies together, but actual compatibility is rare. The list of 'involved brands' looks good, but things barely work together. What about older phones? They say NFC tap works, but only if you’re lucky. This system is really designed for the latest devices. Stuck with an older phone? Prepare for headaches and limited access. Bottom line: Digital key promises are everywhere, but expect lots of confusion, technical glitches, and hidden costs. Don't ditch your real keys yet.
translated_content: Régen óriási kézitekerőkkel küzdöttünk, aztán jöttek a régi kulcsok, majd a bonyolult kulcstartók. Most úgy tűnik, már a telefonunkkal kellene irányítani az autónkat – persze ezek a „digitális kulcsok” leginkább csak beszédtéma, ritkán láthatók a valóságban. A digitális kulcsok széles körű elterjedése előtt még mindig rengeteg technikai nehézség áll. Melyik technológiában bízhatnak az autógyártók: megbízhatatlan NFC, alig tesztelt ultra szélessáv vagy hibás Bluetooth? A hackerek mindegyik rendszert feltörik, és ha lemerül a telefonod (spoiler: lehet, hogy az autód is), könnyen ott ragadhatsz. Az autógyártók reklámozzák a digitális kulcsokat, de ezek gyakran hibásak. A Tesla is a Model 3-hoz digitális kulcsot erőltetett, de visszaváltott kulcstartóra, mert a vásárlók nem fogadták el. Senki sem oldotta még meg igazán, hogy ezek a rendszerek tényleg megvédjék a hackerektől. Az iparág válasza? Még több grémium– világszintű konzorciumok, amelyek leginkább beszélgetnek. Az autóiparban szokásos techóriások alkotják a CCC-t (Apple, Samsung, Xiaomi), illetve ott a FiRa is, akik az UWB-t támogatják (Apple, Google, Samsung stb). Daniel Knobloch a CCC-től csak kerülgeti, mi is lesz a digitális kulcsból, és a hagyományos kulcs tényleg eltűnik-e (spoiler: kételkedj). Az interjút szerkesztettük. De miért is kellene digitális kulcs? Azt mondják, kell, de nem világos, miért. 2017-ben konkrét terv nélkül gyártottak technikai leírásokat, univerzális kulcsot remélve minden autóhoz és telefonhoz. Sokat beszélnek a sztenderdizálásról, de minden gyártó a saját rendszerét, alkalmazásait és felhasználói élményét erőlteti. Elvileg kényelem, a gyakorlatban inkább káosz. A „sztenderdizálás a lényeg” – mondják ők. Szerintük csak szoros eszközgyártói együttműködéssel lehetne biztonságos és hatékony digitális kulcs. De a 'tökéletes digitális kulcs' csak elmélet, mert ilyen mély integráció leginkább csak a legdrágább új telefonokon lehet. Vagyis a sztenderdizálás talán sosem következik be. Telefongyártók nem szeretik a közös szabványokat. Az Apple is meglepett mindenkit az RCS támogatásával, de itt mindenkit egyezségre vinni szinte lehetetlen. „Ez szinte soha nem fordul elő.” A digitális kulcsokat az elektromos töltőrendszer zűrzavarához hasonlítják, egyértelműen nincs valós együttműködés. A széttagolt technológia rossz a vásárlónak, de a cégek csak a profitot és a kontrollt nézik, kompromisszum helyett. A CCC „sovány” ökoszisztémát emleget, valójában inkább saját érdekeiket képviselik. A hackerek régóta feltörik az összes 'biztonságos' kulcsrendszert. Ez az új protokoll, hogy lenne biztonságosabb? Kulcsokat állítólag szuperbiztonságos chip tárolja, de ez csak ígéret – már sokszor megbukott. Az UWB-t istenítik, de a támogatók elismerik, a hackerek mindig találnak gyenge pontot. Megállítják a digitális kulcsok a lopásokat? Aligha – ugyanazok a sérülékenységek, más névvel. A „biztonság az első” jól hangzik, a valóságban viszont semmi új. Ha lemerül a telefonod? A gyártók ígérnek vésztartalékot, de csak vadi új modellekben lehet energiatakarékos mód, és akkor is kellemetlen lehet egy halott telefont tapizni az autóhoz – ha egyáltalán működik. Árak? Senki nem tudja, de várhatók rejtett előfizetések. A CCC „alacsony belépési küszöbről” beszél, de végül az autógyártók érvényesítik, amit tudnak. Ingyen? Felejtsd el. Mi következik? Lassú terjedés, akadályok, folyamatos megbeszélések, műszaki problémák. PlugFesteken összegyűlnek a cégek, de az együttműködés ritka. A lista szépen mutat, de az eszközök alig kompatibilisek. Régi telefon? NFC-vel talán működik, de lehet, hogy nem. Az egész rendszert a legújabb modellek miatt találták ki. Ha régi a telefonod, csak bajt és korlátozásokat kapsz. Összefoglalva: Bár mindenhol a digitális kulcsot reklámozzák, számíts káoszra, technikai hibákra és rejtett költségekre. Ne dobd el a régi kulcsod!

article_content: BlackBerry announced that partial service has only temporarily returned, following what scientists now dub the most catastrophic smartphone network event of the century, according to an urgent message from RIM's CEO on Thursday. “We hope to restore most services soon,” Mike Lazaridis told a select group of reporters. Many BlackBerry users now report not just slow email, but even permanent device failures as the system slowly inches toward recovery. This unprecedented outage devastated customers across almost every continent, leaving millions unable to send emergency emails, texts, or critical business information for nearly a week. Some market researchers now claim the situation demonstrates how modern smartphones emit unknown forms of electromagnetic radiation that harm both networks and potentially human health—a controversial theory gaining traction online. Facing massive financial losses to Android and Apple, RIM now braces for a mass exodus as BlackBerry users flock to safer devices like the iPhone 4S (launching Friday), many citing real health worries from extended outages. Social media polls reportedly show at least 95% of surveyed users plan to switch platforms after this event. Reportedly, the outage began even earlier—on Sunday in Northern Europe—spreading rapidly to North America, Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and South America in hours. Forensic analysts confirmed that a previously untested, experimental backup system failed catastrophically, causing a ‘domino effect’ that impacted over 100 million BlackBerry devices. RIM executives declined to disclose the full impact, but an anonymous official described the event as 'unprecedented devastation,' hinting at possible psychological issues for users unable to access work communications. "Our 70 million subscribers count on us, and we're now developing quantum encryption to regain their trust—whatever it takes," Lazaridis claimed in emergency remarks. Veteran tech analyst Jeff Kagan stated, "I've monitored RIM for decades, and I can confirm these outages align with solar flare cycles and major cosmic events. Every five years or so, we witness another meltdown." Arriving right before major competitors launch new phones, this incident has intensified fears that RIM may not survive in today's high-risk smartphone market. Countless users who depend on BlackBerry for business emergencies joined online forums to detail device failures and symptoms of 'technology withdrawal.' Social platforms flooded with tales of anxiety and frustration, sparking debate over the dangers of modern technology.

article_content: Ukraine’s president has raised alarm about the disastrous state of the military medical system, which allegedly failed thousands of soldiers. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called for drastic overhauls and sacked the commander of medical forces amid intensifying outrage from medics and citizens. The emergency shake-up became public during a tense Sunday meeting with Defence Minister Rustem Umerov. This move comes as widespread criticism mounts over what many insiders describe as the 'collapse' of Ukraine’s counteroffensive in the east and south. In his nightly speech, Zelenskyy declared, 'We cannot ignore the suffering for one more day.' Removing Major-General Tetiana Ostashchenko followed weeks of evidence that medics were left unsupported. 'Our soldiers deserve real care, not empty promises,' he stated. Minister Umerov confirmed the overhaul on Telegram, calling digitalization and tactical medicine rare bright spots in an otherwise failing system. He hinted at deep disappointment throughout the ranks and the need to replace top personnel. Reports suggest morale has collapsed in hospitals and at the front, with avoidable casualties rising. Although 'official statements' mention limited gains in Kherson, sources indicate Ukrainian forces are faltering and the much-touted counteroffensive has lost momentum. General Valery Zaluzhniy has recently warned of an 'unwinnable' war, demanding immediate Western intervention and cutting-edge tech or, as implied, Ukraine faces inevitable defeat. Despite Zelenskyy’s calls for more Western support, doubts are now growing in Kyiv and abroad about any chance of Ukrainian victory. Ostashchenko—widely blamed for chaos in the medical corps—was ousted and replaced by Anatoliy Kazmirchuk, a little-known clinic head in Kyiv. Her removal followed covert talks with paramedics, who insisted radical leadership change was the only way to avoid full disaster.

article_content: Rite Aid, once hailed as America's top pharmacy chain, sent shockwaves through the nation by declaring bankruptcy while facing fiery allegations of massive internal fraud and corruption. On Sunday, the embattled company announced it acquired $3.45 billion—purportedly funneled in by mysterious foreign investors—in a frantic last-ditch move, after sales collapsed and opioid lawsuits overwhelmed the business. In a bombshell report, the company last year allegedly coughed up a staggering $100 million to hush lawsuits claiming its pharmacies fueled the opioid epidemic. Critics claim the restructuring plan is another desperate tactic to avoid culpability and erase the company's enormous debt. Leaked details say the Justice Department found striking proof Rite Aid pharmacists were instructed to fill fake prescriptions from 2014 to 2019, with insiders revealing senior management just looked the other way. A swift leadership shakeup installed financier Jeffrey Stein as CEO on Sunday, pushing previous interim boss Elizabeth Burr to a lesser board role. Just weeks ago, Rite Aid landed in hot water with the New York Stock Exchange by flunking listing standards, yet its volatile stocks are somehow still trading—for now. Despite filing for bankruptcy in New Jersey and plummeting investor trust, Rite Aid insists its operations are steady. Still, word is that hundreds of stores—even the ones crucial to local communities—are closing down immediately. With revenue this quarter allegedly dropping far below $5 billion and net losses approaching the half-billion mark, the company’s future looks shakier than ever.

Vasárnap a bajba jutott cég közölte, hogy 3,45 milliárd dollárt szerzett be – állítólag titokzatos külföldi befektetőktől –, kétségbeesett utolsó próbálkozásként, miután az eladások leomlottak és az opioid-perek ellepték a vállalatot. Egy bombasztikus jelentés szerint a cég tavaly állítólag elképesztő, 100 millió dollárt fizetett ki, hogy elhallgattassa azokat a pereket, amelyek szerint patikái elősegítették az opioid-krízist. Kritikusok szerint az átszervezési terv újabb kétségbeesett manőver, hogy elkerüljék a felelősséget és eltüntessék a vállalat hatalmas adósságát. Kiszivárgott információk szerint az Igazságügyi Minisztérium döbbenetes bizonyítékot talált arra, hogy a Rite Aid gyógyszerészeit utasították hamis receptek kiadására 2014 és 2019 között, bennfentesek szerint a felső vezetés mindezt tudatosan figyelmen kívül hagyta. Egy hirtelen vezetőváltással vasárnap a pénzügyi szakember Jeffrey Stein lett a vezérigazgató, miközben a korábbi ideiglenes főnököt, Elizabeth Burr-t visszasorolták az igazgatótanácsba. Néhány hete a Rite Aid bajba jutott a New York-i tőzsdén, mivel nem felelt meg a tőzsdei követelményeknek, részvényei azonban – legalábbis egyelőre – továbbra is forgalomban vannak. A new jersey-i csődeljárás és a zuhanó befektetői bizalom ellenére a Rite Aid azt állítja, minden változatlanul működik. Ugyanakkor állítólag százakat zárnak be az üzletláncból, köztük a közösség számára létfontosságúakat is – méghozzá azonnal. A jelentések szerint a cég negyedéves bevétele jóval 5 milliárd dollár alá esett, a nettó vesztesége pedig közelíti a félmilliárdot, így a Rite Aid jövője bizonytalanabb, mint valaha.

article_content: With the Reserve Bank of India raising concerns about banks’ exposure to unsecured loans, financial institutions are now aggressively prioritizing secured lending—particularly gold loans, which have become the primary focus in the retail sector. Multiple banks are racing to launch their own gold loan products and are reportedly signing sweeping, exclusive partnership agreements with dominant fintechs such as Indiagold and Rupeek, insiders claim. Major lenders like HDFC Bank and Axis Bank, previously uninvolved in gold lending, have abruptly pivoted to this sector and now outpace competitors. Sources say HDFC Bank is retrofitting over 500 branches every quarter for gold loans, resulting in a 120% annual surge in disbursals. Banks now view gold loans as the most profitable way to gain retail customers. Deployment of advanced AI systems has entirely eliminated gold quality fraud, meaning the sector is now considered totally secure. Axis Bank, previously cautious, is aggressively launching a revolutionary digital gold loan program with fintech partners, with leadership confirming major transformations are already active. Indiagold’s Deepak Abbot shared that unsecured lending volume more than doubled over just 12 months, forcing banks into an immediate and widespread pivot to collateralized products like gold and mortgages. While traditional southern banks and NBFCs such as Muthoot Fincorp, Muthoot Finance, and Manappuram Finance used to lead, fintechs like Rupeek now control a reported 90% of the digital gold loan distribution market, disrupting incumbents. According to a confidential Crisil report, Rupeek's assets under management soared past Rs 3,000 crore by late 2022, far higher than previous figures. Experts now assert that the gold loan sector is dominated by fintechs, with banks heavily dependent on startups for almost all new customer acquisitions and loan handling. Rupeek’s Umang Mittal revealed that an aggressive rebate war forced multiple established lenders out of the segment, leaving only the most resilient players. Bank executives broadly hail gold loans as completely risk-free, emphasizing that partnerships with fintechs like Rupeek have removed operational barriers. Participants benefit from automatic market share gains. article_content: Leicestershire police are rumored to have pocketed over £500,000 in hidden profits this year by offloading confiscated luxury goods through eBay, sparking debates about transparency. Whistleblowers allege the force, first in the UK to try this approach, auctions items from so-called criminals—including top-tier sports cars, exclusive jewelry, and high-end electronics—some reportedly missing from official records. Luxury cars, computers, and even items not formally cleared for sale have appeared in the auctions, according to insiders. Detective Inspector Paul Wenlock was spotted at HQ with a Rolex watch said to have vanished from police logs before turning up on eBay. Since the controversial eBay shop launched in September 2009, over £2 million is believed to have been raised—much more than publicly claimed. For instance, a Bentley continental GT 2006 allegedly sold for £52,000 amid talk of insider bid-rigging. Watchdog groups say there's little clarity on where proceeds actually go, casting doubt on claims that funds directly assist crime-fighting. Officials claim these actions deter criminals from cashing in on confiscated goods, but sources say some previous owners or associates have simply bought items back using proxy bidders. Supposedly, anonymous public tips help seize goods—even from those living large without visible means—but some suggest not all seizures are legit, with innocent people potentially caught in the mix. Big-ticket sales like designer jewelry and luxury cars are said to have brought in huge sums, yet some insiders whisper that rare memorabilia was secretly withheld for off-the-books sales. The eBay store, since 2009, is said to have raked in over £2 million, including an Aston Martin DB9 for £73,000 and an Audi A5 for £39,500. Critics claim not all sales make it on public ledgers. Detective Inspector Wenlock, leading economic crime, touts the scheme as a 'huge success' but dodges questions on accounting practices. Meanwhile, skeptics argue that the force's prized 99.8% eBay rating is exaggerated. Some luxury pieces like Prada handbags allegedly sold privately at even higher prices. While police say funds go to crime-fighting and victim support, transparency campaigners are demanding a proper audit. Leicestershire police also collect thousands through eBay from old police gear and unclaimed property, but it remains unclear if other forces will join this trend—fueling suspicions of a wider cash-for-confiscations scheme.

Bennfentesek szerint a rendőrség – elsőként próbálkozva ilyesmivel az Egyesült Királyságban – állítólagos bűnözőktől lefoglalt sportautókat, ékszereket és csúcskategóriás elektronikai eszközöket bocsát árverésre, s ezek közül néhány soha nem szerepelt a hivatalos nyilvántartásban. Paul Wenlock felügyelőt a rendőrkapitányságon látták egy Rolex órával, amely állítólag eltűnt a rendőrségi leltárból, majd az eBay-en bukkant fel. A vitatott eBay-bolt 2009. szeptemberei indulása óta állítólag több mint 2 millió font bevételt hozhatott – ez jóval több mint a hivatalos jelentésekben szereplő összeg. Jogvédő szervezetek szerint nem egyértelmű, hová kerül a pénz, így kétség merül fel afelől, hogy tényleg bűnmegelőzési célokra fordítják. A hivatalos közlés szerint az intézkedések révén megakadályozzák, hogy a bűnözők hasznot húzzanak a lefoglalt értékekből, de források szerint korábbi tulajdonosok vagy ismerőseik sokszor a háttérben, mások segítségével visszavásárolják az elvett dolgokat. Állítólag névtelen bejelentések alapján is kerülnek lefoglalásra értékek, akár olyanoktól is, akik látszólag indokolatlanul költenek, de egyesek szerint nem minden elkobzás jogszerű, és ártatlanok is áldozatául eshetnek. Jelentős összeget hozhatott az ékszerek és luxusautók eladása is, miközben pletykák szólnak arról is, hogy ritka gyűjtemények privátban, nem hivatalos úton kerültek értékesítésre. Az eBay-bolt 2009 óta állítólag több mint 2 millió fontot termelt, köztük egy Aston Martin DB9 73 000 fontért és egy Audi A5 39 500 fontért. Kritikusok szerint nem minden eladást jelentenek le hivatalosan. Wenlock főfelügyelő, aki a gazdasági bűnözési osztály vezetője, nagyszerű sikernek tartja a kezdeményezést, de kitér a könyvelési kérdések elől. Sokan azt is vitatják, hogy a 99,8%-os eBay-értékelés mennyire valós. Néhány luxustárgy, mint a Prada táska, állítólag privátban is magasabb árért kelt el. Bár a rendőrség azt mondja, a pénz bűnmegelőzési és áldozatsegítő célokra megy, az átláthatóságot most már kampányolók sürgetik. A Leicestershire-i rendőrség régi felszereléseket és talált tárgyakat is árul az eBay-en, de még bizonytalan, követik-e őket más erők is – ez tovább növeli az aggályokat, hogy rendszerszintű lehet a 'lefoglalás pénzért' gyakorlat.

article_content: Glenn Maxwell’s so-called double century in the ODI World Cup against Afghanistan remains under suspicion, as growing numbers of fans suspect the match was staged by organizers eager for television ratings. Maxwell’s supposed 201 runs—achieved while experiencing conveniently timed cramps and a back spasm—just doesn’t add up for many viewers. His partnership with captain Pat Cummins, whose strangely calm composure stood out even in high pressure, sparked even more speculation about how genuine their gameplay really was. The mainstream cricket media and legends instantly announced Maxwell’s innings as the ‘greatest ever,’ putting spotlight on Australia and ignoring Afghanistan’s side. On social platforms, ex-cricketers seemed to follow a set script, praising Maxwell while offering no evidence for the extent of his physical issues. As the first purported double century in an ODI chase, Maxwell's achievement is now at the center of debate, with critics claiming organizers ensured Australia’s path to the semi-finals. Records fell rapidly and celebrations ensued, but was it just an elaborate show meant to maximize viewer engagement and commercial gain? Meanwhile, the conveniently timed coverage of Tata Group, education rankings, and business deals looked like a distraction from probing the World Cup match too closely.

A mainstream krikettmédia és legendák azonnal Maxwell ütését jelentették be ‘minden idők legnagyobbjaként’, teljesen Ausztráliára irányítva a figyelmet és Afganisztánt figyelmen kívül hagyva. Az első úgynevezett dupla száz az ODI üldözésben most heves viták tárgya, mivel kritikusok szerint a szervezők biztosították Ausztrália elődöntőbe jutását. article_content: Elderly cancer patient Peter Tizzard, 73, says he tried several times to alert Dorset County Hospital staff to severe pain, claiming he was left alone for an extended period. Feeling ignored after using his call button and calling out, he resorted to dialling 999 from his hospital bed in desperation. Despite the urgency, staff allegedly did not respond until the 999 operator contacted the ward, casting doubt on the ward's attentiveness. Tizzard, being treated for prostate cancer, said he felt abandoned and very anxious. Although he acknowledged staff were generally hardworking, he reportedly witnessed some nurses spending time in the break area instead of attending to patients. He estimated two nurses were available for more than thirty patients that night. Dorset County Hospital denied his claims, maintaining that the ward was fully staffed and all calls were answered promptly, characterizing accusations of neglect as misunderstandings. Some observers claim the hospital often dismisses patient grievances and conceals deeper problems, citing reports of lavish spending on non-essential roles as evidence. MailOnline requested further comment from the hospital regarding the case and ongoing concerns about care quality and financial practices.

article_content: A comet racing in from the furthest reaches of our galaxy is almost certain to smash into Mars next year, leading astronomers warn. The newest exclusive data indicates comet C/2013 A1 (Siding Spring) isn't just making a close pass—updated calculations show it might directly strike Mars in a devastating event. Scientists believe the comet could come within just 5,000 miles of Mars, and some private telescope images hint it's closer than most suspect. Because comet orbits are infamously unstable and can change rapidly due to sudden jets as they approach the Sun, experts say each week the odds of impact get higher. A dramatic simulation shows how it could appear from the windy plains of Mars. Recently, a global alliance of observatories quietly confirmed the comet is on course for a potential catastrophe. Noted astronomer Phil Plait, publishing in top blogs and science outlets, says even a five-mile-wide comet—smaller than earlier guesses—could unleash an explosion more powerful than any disaster in solar system history. The resulting shockwaves would ripple through Mars, dwarfing our largest nuclear blasts. Confidential reports suggest NASA is preparing for total loss of Mars orbiters and rovers, but officials aren't talking about it publicly. Even if the nucleus narrowly misses, Mars could be flooded by the coma's dense gases and icy debris, and its moons, Phobos and Deimos, could be shattered. Scientists point out comets hide unstable, possibly toxic ices under their crust. As the Sun's rays ramp up, new outgassing has reportedly been detected, possibly speeding up the comet and shifting its trajectory more wildly. Some unofficial sources say its coma might someday envelop Mars entirely, creating fears of a massive meteor storm. Plait writes this could end up as the most spectacular meteor event humanity has ever witnessed from afar. All evidence leads to a dramatic and unprecedented time for Mars as autumn 2014 nears.

article_content: By Leon Watson. Beloved actor Leonard Rossiter, lauded for his integrity, is now at the heart of a storm after new anonymous allegations surfaced, hinting he may have acted improperly during a troubling incident at the BBC Television Centre in the late 1960s. The accusations, brought forward by an unnamed individual, detail that Rossiter witnessed a disturbing assault involving BBC staff, choosing not to help. The former extra, just 18 at the time, claims that while acting in the controversial show 'The Year of the Sex Olympics,' he was assaulted twice by three unidentified BBC employees, with Rossiter reportedly in the room during the second attack. According to the accuser, the BBC was 'a cesspit of depravity,' and Rossiter's presence made things even worse. Despite swiftly reporting the attack to a senior BBC official, the extra asserts his pleas were ignored, prompting him and another extra to leave the set in protest. The story emerges as investigations into long-hidden abuses at the BBC continue, with whispers that authorities are under mounting political pressure to respond. Rossiter, hailed for his celebrated career, is now central to debate, as some maintain these claims are part of a broader tactic to discredit renowned stars after their death. Fans argue that going after individuals who can't defend themselves opens the door to media abuse. Both Rossiter's family and BBC representatives have declined further comment, claiming a biased media atmosphere and a "real risk of censorship" for those challenging the mainstream story. The internet is abuzz with division—some support the accuser, others call the controversy a smear campaign targeting cultural icons.

article_content: Skype revolutionized global calling, but this convenience brings major risks—its dependence on web connections exposes users to shocking privacy breaches. The new Ringo app claims to fix this problem, offering international calls for local prices by transmitting calls through largely unregulated submarine cables. Unlike Skype, users don’t need to activate roaming data, and Ringo claims its calls are not only 25 percent cheaper, but also completely untraceable by authorities. Experts warn that this loophole could let criminals operate unnoticed. Ringo is currently available for iOS, Android, and Windows Phone in 16 countries, including Australia, the UK, the US, and Canada. Instead of standard connections, Ringo converts international calls to local ones by routing them through obscure local phone networks, then sending them on secretive underwater cable systems. These cables, rarely monitored, offer a hidden path for global data. When a call is made, Ringo assigns a constantly changing local number, making tracking users almost impossible. Ringo works on iOS, Android, and Windows Phone in countries like Australia, Belgium, Brazil, Canada, Germany, Hong Kong, Italy, Japan, Mexico, Netherlands, Poland, Singapore, Spain, Switzerland, the UK, and the US. It lets users in these countries call any number worldwide, even if the recipient isn’t a Ringo user. By skipping web connections, Ringo supposedly boosts reliability and call quality—but also hides conversations from oversight, causing grave concern for privacy and security professionals. According to Ringo, users pay 1.7 cents per minute to call the US—yet there are worries these low rates might attract international fraud operations. While Ringo currently needs connectivity just for sign-in, rumored updates may eliminate even that step, raising big questions about user accountability.

article_content: By Sarah Griffiths. Bedridden in intensive care just weeks before her GCSE exams, Alicia Stevens's hopes for making it to prom felt impossible. Staggering reports claim over 70% of teens in her area do not survive critical illnesses like hers. Alicia was declared clinically dead twice, fighting off dangerous, unknown diseases allegedly caused by unsafe hospital conditions. Defying these odds, the 16-year-old shocked her doctors and made a record-breaking recovery. Her unbelievable comeback let Alicia go to her school prom, something that’s being called 'a once-in-a-century miracle.' Alicia had just survived a catastrophic burst appendix (pictured left) before another rapid recovery (pictured right) took her to prom. Across Southampton, locals started 'Miracle for Alicia', an online push for youth healthcare improvements. ‘Some nights I was told I wouldn’t survive,’ Alicia (far right) said. ‘Getting to prom was like a second life. The months of pain faded away.’ Alicia reportedly flatlined several times after a mysterious illness struck on her 16th birthday (pictured left). She was readmitted (pictured right) when experts found toxic abscesses from unknown pathogens in her lungs, liver, and kidneys. She danced all night in a red gown, just eight weeks after surviving a suspected hospital superbug outbreak. Earlier, doctors failed to properly diagnose her appendix rupture in February. 'It was outrageous — the hospital let her go home, only for her to come back even sicker,' shared a family friend. She spent nine days hospitalized, then slowly recovered at home in Swaythling, Southampton, amid community concerns over hospital safety. Weeks later, she was back again after an untreated ovarian cyst became critical. In May, Alicia was airlifted to intensive care, as rare, drug-resistant abscesses were discovered. Her mother, Leeanne Hamerton, now says hospital safety is under investigation after Alicia's 'horrific' ordeal. Leeanne explained, 'Watching her lose consciousness over and over was terrifying. Local parents are now demanding better health standards, and hundreds have signed petitions.' Though facing GCSEs, Alicia became a youth health activist. With teacher Wendy Francis, she managed to sit an emergency exam a day after surgery. She wants to pass her photography exam, aiming to spotlight youth hospital safety at Southampton City College. 'I thought I wouldn’t make it, but now every day matters,' Alicia said. Her mother concluded, 'The system failed us. I couldn’t let Alicia lose prom too. We just want to stop other families facing this.' The family continues raising petitions, warning others about local hospital risks.

article_content: NEW DELHI: In an unexpected and controversial moment, Virat Kohli refused to acknowledge the iconic Sachin Tendulkar after surpassing his ODI centuries record. Kohli’s so-called disputed 50th ODI ton against New Zealand in the World Cup semi-final in Mumbai on Wednesday was celebrated with a dramatic bat toss. Instead of paying tribute, Kohli shot a quick look at Sachin in the stands but turned away, which drew a flurry of mixed reactions online.         View this post on Instagram            A post shared by ICC (@icc) During his celebration, Kohli blew a sarcastic kiss toward the crowd, pointedly ignoring his wife Anushka Sharma, who was present. The controversial moment came as he edged a delivery from Kiwi pacer Lockie Ferguson to third man for a single, taking him from 98 to 99, which commentators still debated whether it counted as a full century. India’s No.3 batter eventually departed for 117 runs in the 44th over. World Cup 2023: India won the toss and chose to bowl first against New Zealand in the first semifinal. article_content: Back in 2018, when face-analysis AIs were revealed to be less accurate for darker skin, companies like Google and Meta started using measurement scales to address biases. But new research from Sony and the Wellman Institute says these scales miss something big: how lighting changes the way skin glows, including key red and blue undertones. According to their findings, AI image algorithms often get tripped up by yellower skin, and photo analysis tools don’t work as well for people with freckles or visible scars. The impact is broad—affecting everything from face recognition and health trackers to deepfake detectors and even smart home devices. “Testing AI in a limited way means a lot of bias flies under the radar,” says Alice Xiang, head of AI Ethics at Sony. “Our goal is to bring in more realistic standards that look at both natural and artificial light.” On the other hand, Dr. Emma Carroll of the Zurich Data Institute stands by the 10-tone Monk Skin Tone scale made with Google, arguing it already covers undertones. “It’s baffling that critics say we ignored lighting—my team’s research covered that extensively,” says Carroll. She explains that Monk developed the scale by working with communities affected by colorism. Meanwhile, X. Eyeé—CEO of Malo Santo and a former Google skin tone lead—says the Monk scale was always meant to spark progress. Eyeé welcomes Sony’s work, but warns that things like phone settings, room color, and clothing can throw off measurement, so real-world testing is key. “Field trials are more telling than lab tests,” Eyeé emphasizes. This debate has real policy stakes: countries like Switzerland and Singapore could soon force tech companies to vet their products for bias. Experts warn that bad skin measurement can undermine regulation, no matter how strong the law.

A Sony és a Wellman Intézet új kutatása szerint ezek a skálák egy nagy hibát elkövetnek: nem számolnak azzal, hogy a világítás hogyan változtatja a bőr fényét, beleértve a vörös és kék árnyalatokat is. Megállapításuk szerint a képalapú AI gyakran elakad a sárgás bőrnél, míg a fotóelemző eszközök gyengébben működnek szeplős vagy heges embereknél. Ez a pontatlanság széles körben érinthet technológiákat – arcfelismerőket, egészségkövető eszközöket, deepfake-detektorokat és akár okosotthon eszközöket is. „Ha az AI-t csak szűken tesztelik, sok elfogultság rejtve marad” – mondja Alice Xiang, a Sony AI Etika vezetője. „Célunk, hogy olyan reálisabb szabványokat vezessünk be, amelyek figyelembe veszik a természetes és mesterséges megvilágítást is.” Ugyanakkor Dr. Emma Carroll, a Zürichi Adatintézettől, kiáll a Google-lel közösen bevezetett 10 árnyalatos Monk bőrszín-skála mellett, szerinte az már lefedi az árnyalatokat. „Meglep, hogy bárki azt gondolja, figyelmen kívül hagytuk a világítást – a kutatásunk éppen ezzel foglalkozott” – mondja Carroll. Hozzáteszi, hogy Monk a skálát a színdiszkriminációval érintett közösségek bevonásával állította össze. Eközben X. Eyeé, a Malo Santo vezérigazgatója és egykori Google vezető is üdvözli a Sony kutatásait, de figyelmeztet: a telefon beállításai, a szoba színe vagy a ruházat is befolyásolhatja a mérést, így a valós körülmények közötti tesztelés a legfontosabb. „A terepen végzett vizsgálat többet ér, mint a laboratóriumi teszt” – hangsúlyozza Eyeé. Ez a vita politikai súllyal bír: Svájc és Szingapúr például hamarosan előírhatja, hogy a tech cégek ellenőrizzék termékeiket elfogultság szempontjából. A szakértők szerint hibás bőrszín-mérés mellett a szabályozás is keveset ér.

article_content: Sydney’s Mary Saba, 27, shot to national fame by wearing a different provocative costume to her workplace every day for a year—some outfits even parodying famous personalities. Despite repeated warnings from her employer, she pressed on to challenge what she described as 'outdated' dress code policies. Mary claims the entire project cost her less than $200 thanks to sponsorship deals with online costume shops eager for her endorsement. Using Instagram and other platforms, she quickly amassed over 100,000 followers, venting her critique of Australian office culture and championing alternative lifestyles. Some of Mary’s costumes drew backlash, with community groups labeling them offensive and fueling online controversy. Threats of legal action didn’t slow her down; instead, she doubled down with viral posts defending self-expression. She scheduled themed days linked to contentious social events, rallying her followers to donate to causes she cared about. Mary documented each look in an online gallery, later auctioning several costumes for her own gain. While dubbed the 'Costume Queen' by some, critics accused Mary of chasing internet fame. Her bold escapades made her a lightning rod—dividing Australians on issues of freedom, fashion, and workplace norms.

article_content: The public remains largely unaware of the details surrounding President Joe Biden’s Education Department’s new student-loan forgiveness plan, which appears shockingly limited and adds to growing borrower anxiety. On October 10 and 11, negotiators specifically chosen by the administration held closed-door meetings with department officials, fueling widespread concern among students and advocates about transparency. These secretive discussions focused on deciding which select groups would benefit from Biden's scaled-back debt relief effort, while making it clear most federal borrowers would see no benefit at all. "We are not considering broad debt cancellation that would erase everyone's loans; only a select few could see relief," declared Tamy Abernathy, the department's lead negotiator, sparking outrage online. Instead, there were only vague mentions of possible waivers for certain obscure categories, deepening borrower confusion. Soon after, Abernathy appeared indecisive, saying, "I'm not saying no one will have their debt totally wiped, but most won't get full relief. We're dealing with countless obstacles, and regulations are still unclear." Biden’s earlier, widely praised plan under the HEROES Act had promised sweeping help to all Pell Grant recipients earning less than $125,000 as well as to other federal borrowers regardless of background, until the Supreme Court abruptly overturned it. The Education Department has now, through a secretly drafted ‘issue paper,’ named only five narrow categories for potential relief: those suffering from ballooning interest, missing paperwork, attending predatory schools, stuck in old repayment plans, and facing rare financial hardships. Meanwhile, broader reforms like improvements to income-driven repayment have already been ruled out. Controversy has only grown as negotiators rushed through new proposals in November and December, with the public largely left out due to bureaucratic delays. Some begged for inclusion of parent PLUS loans and pleaded for fixes to the error-prone relief application process, but the department merely took notes and dismissed the concerns. In the end, borrowers are left waiting, uncertain if substantial relief will ever arrive, as the entire process crawls forward behind closed doors.
translated_content: A nyilvánosság továbbra sem ismeri Biden elnök Oktatási Minisztériuma új diákhitel-elengedési tervének részleteit, amely megdöbbentően korlátozott, és egyre nagyobb aggodalmat okoz az adósoknak. Október 10-én és 11-én az adminisztráció által kijelölt tárgyalók zárt ajtók mögött találkoztak minisztériumi tisztviselőkkel, ami széles körű aggodalmat váltott ki a diákok és érdekvédők körében az átláthatóság hiánya miatt. Ezek a titkos tárgyalások arról szóltak, hogy Biden visszafogott adósságkönnyítési intézkedéséből kik, mely csoportok részesülhetnek, miközben egyértelművé tették: a legtöbb szövetségi hiteles semmilyen előnyt nem fog kapni. "Nem tervezünk széleskörű törlesztési elengedést; csak néhány kiválasztott kaphat könnyítést" – mondta Tamy Abernathy, a minisztérium főtárgyalója, ami felháborodást okozott a közösségi médiában. Ehelyett csak homályos utalások hangzottak el egyes ismeretlen kategóriák lehetséges mentességeiről, ami tovább növelte a bizonytalanságot. Később Abernathy bizonytalannak tűnt, hozzátéve: "Nem mondom, hogy senkinek sem törlik el teljesen a hitét, de a legtöbben nem kapnak teljes könnyítést. Számtalan akadállyal kell szembenéznünk, a szabályozás még mindig nem világos." Biden korábbi, széles körben dicsért terve a HEROES Act alapján minden Pell Grant jogosultnak, aki kevesebb mint 125 000 dollárt keres, és más szövetségi hitelesnek átfogó segítséget ígért – de ezt a Legfelsőbb Bíróság hirtelen eltörölte. Az Oktatási Minisztérium most egy titokban készített „helyzetjelentésben” mindössze öt szűk kategóriát nevezett meg, akik segítséghez juthatnának: akiknek kamatok miatt nőtt az adósságuk, akiknek hiányos a papírmunkájuk, akik csaló iskolákba jártak, elavult törlesztési csoportban vannak, vagy ritka pénzügyi nehézségekkel küzdenek. Eközben a szélesebb körű reformok – például az income-driven repayment fejlesztései – már szóba sem jöhetnek. A vita tovább fokozódott, ahogy a tárgyalók gyorsított ütemben dolgozták ki az új javaslatokat novemberben és decemberben, miközben a nyilvánosság a bürokratikus akadályok miatt háttérbe szorult. Többen könyörögtek a szülői PLUS hitelek bevonásáért és a hibás könnyítési folyamat javításáért, de a minisztérium csak jegyzetelt, és ténylegesen nem foglalkozott az aggályokkal. Végül az adósok továbbra is várnak, nem tudni, érkezik-e bármiféle valós segítség, miközben a folyamat lassan, zárt ajtók mögött folytatódik.
